title: Ford Fairlane Engines by Year (1955–1970)
description: Every factory engine in the Ford Fairlane by year, 1955–1970: Y-block V8s incl. the supercharged 312, the FE 352 and 390, the 427 and the 428 Cobra Jet.
intro: Ford used the Fairlane name on its top full-size series from 1955 to 1961 and on its mid-size car from 1962 to 1970, after which the Torino took over.
Pick a year to see every engine offered that model year, with its code, rated horsepower and the trims it came in. Each engine links to its full specs.
The full-size Fairlane offered Ford's six and Y-block V8s, including a supercharged 312 in 1957, then the FE-series 332 and 352 and, for 1961, the 390.
The mid-size Fairlane introduced Ford's small-block V8 as the 221 and 260, followed by the 289, including the 271 hp high-performance version.
The 1966 redesign made room for the 390 FE, and the 427 was offered in 1966–1967. From 1968 the Fairlane shared the Torino's engines, including the 428 and 429 Cobra Jets.

excluded.researchNote: Ford's 1955 brochures list only the 223 six and 272 V-8, and The Classic Ford's 1955 engine page lists no 292 for Ford cars. The 292 (193 hp manual / 198 hp automatic) was the Thunderbird engine and also went into police Interceptor packages. Show it as a police/special-order item, not a regular Fairlane option.

sources.name: Over-Drive Magazine 1957 Ford cars fact sheet

excluded.researchNote: Ford's 1957 Fairlane brochure advertises the 285-hp version, but Over-Drive says it went only to selected race teams. Treat it as a racing/special-order tune. Over-Drive also lists a 340-hp NASCAR supercharged 312 (race teams only, one source), which is not added.

excluded.name: 430 V8
excluded.researchNote: NHRA's 1960 'FAIRLANE' block lists a 430/350, but Ford's 1960 car brochures, Over-Drive's 1960 full-size sheet and Wikipedia list no 430 for the Fairlane. The 430 was a Thunderbird engine. Exclude it from the page.

method: Every engine and year listed here was confirmed by at least three independent sources: the NHRA Stock Car Classification Guides, factory material such as GM Heritage Center information kits and sales brochures, EPA records and established references. Several Wikipedia articles count as one source. Where sources give different ratings, the factory figure is shown and the difference is noted. Factory race-only packages need two sources.
